fields.name: recipient_email
fields.label: Send messages to
fields.description: Every message composed by this form is addressed to this inbox. There is no server behind the form: pressing Submit opens the visitor's own mail service with the message filled in, so nothing is stored on the website and nothing is sent until the visitor presses send in their mail app.

fields.name: subject_prefix
fields.label: Subject line starts with
fields.description: The subject of the composed email. The visitor's chosen option from the dropdown below is added on the end — keep the trailing space or dash.

fields.name: subject_field
fields.label: Which field finishes the subject line
fields.description: The "Field name" of one of the fields below, usually the dropdown. Whatever the visitor picks there is added to the end of the subject. Leave empty to always use the fallback.

fields.name: subject_fallback
fields.label: Subject if that field is left empty
fields.description: Used when the visitor did not choose anything.

fields.name: rows
fields.label: Form rows
fields.description: Each row holds one or two fields. Two fields share the row side by side; one field spans the full width. Drag rows to reorder the form. All of the visitor's answers are written into the email in this order.

fields.name: fields
fields.label: Fields in this row
fields.description: One field fills the row. Two sit side by side. More than two will not fit.

fields.name: name
fields.label: Field name
fields.description: The internal name for this field. Lower-case letters, numbers and underscores, no spaces — for example firstname. It is never shown to the visitor. Changing it on an existing field is safe, but if it is named in "Which field finishes the subject line" above, change that too.

fields.name: label
fields.label: Label
fields.description: Shown above the box, and used as the heading for this answer in the email.

fields.name: email_label
fields.label: Name for this answer in the email
fields.description: Optional. Leave empty to use the Label above. Set it when the label is a long question but the email reads better with a short word.

fields.name: type
fields.label: Kind of field
fields.description: "Email" and "Phone" bring up the right keyboard on a phone and check the format. "Dropdown" uses the list of choices below. "Long message" is the tall box, and always goes at the end of the email.

fields.name: placeholder
fields.label: Grey hint inside the box
fields.description: Optional. For a dropdown this is the first, unselected line of the list.

fields.name: autocomplete
fields.label: Autofill hint
fields.description: Optional, and best left alone. Lets the browser fill the box from the visitor's saved details — for example given-name, family-name, email, tel-national.

fields.name: pattern
fields.label: Format check
fields.description: Optional, for experts. A regular expression the answer must match. The phone field uses ^\d{10}$ to require exactly ten digits. Leave empty for no check.

fields.name: choices
fields.label: Dropdown choices
fields.description: Only used when the kind of field is "Dropdown".

fields.name: consent_text
fields.label: Tick-box wording
fields.description: The sentence beside the tick box, usually with a link to the privacy policy. Leave empty to drop the tick box entirely.

fields.name: send_heading
fields.label: Line shown after Submit
fields.description: Submitting opens Gmail in a new tab. This panel then appears under the button with the other ways to send, for visitors who do not use Gmail.

fields.name: send_note
fields.label: Small print under those buttons
fields.description: Optional. Usually the address again, as a plain link.

fields.name: support_label
fields.label: Right-hand panel name for screen readers

fields.name: support_rows
fields.label: Office details
fields.description: The stacked blocks on the right, above the map. Leave the list empty, with no map and no directions link, to drop the right-hand column and let the form run full width.

fields.name: body
fields.label: Text
fields.description: Links are allowed. Use Shift+Enter for a line break inside an address so it stays one block.

fields.label: Map
fields.description: The embed address for the map. In Google Maps open the place, choose Share, then "Embed a map", then Copy HTML, and paste only the part between src=" and the next quote. Leave empty to hide the map.

fields.name: directions_url
fields.label: Directions link
fields.description: Where the button goes — the normal Google Maps link for the place, not the embed address. Leave empty to hide the button.

fields.name: phone

fields.name: website

fields.name: initials
fields.label: Initials
fields.description: The two letters shown in a grey circle when this participant has no logo, or when the logo file is missing. Leave empty to use the first two letters of the name.

fields.name: href
fields.label: Link address
fields.description: A web address, a page of this site such as /resources-tech.html, or a mailto: address. Leave empty for a document that is announced but not published yet — the row shows without a link.

fields.name: categories
fields.label: Live categories
fields.description: The categories this participant is live in. These drive the filter panel. A category missing from the list is added under "Participant categories & roles".

fields.name: parent
fields.label: Sits under
fields.description: Leave empty to make this a top-level category in the filter panel. Otherwise pick the top-level category it belongs to. The panel is two levels deep, so pick one that is itself top-level.

fields.name: roles
fields.label: Roles
fields.description: Pick every role this participant is live in. The table prints the short key for each.

fields.name: role_value
fields.label: Role
fields.description: Exactly as it is written on a participant. Changing it here does not change it on the participants that already use it.

fields.name: role_key
fields.label: Short key
fields.description: What the table prints, for example BNP. Keep it to a few characters.

fields.name: role_full
fields.label: Full name
fields.description: Shown as a tooltip on the short key in the table.

fields.name: areas
fields.label: Areas of the knowledge base
fields.description: Each area is one page of the Resources section. Use + to add one, the item menu to duplicate or delete, and drag to reorder — the order here is the order of the hub cards and the sidebar.

fields.name: summary
fields.label: Short description
fields.description: The line under the title on the hub card and the sub-area cards.

fields.name: icon
fields.label: Icon
fields.description: Shown on this area's card.

fields.name: page
fields.label: Page address
fields.description: Where this area's card and sidebar entry link to, for example /resources-tech.html — or a full web address for an external area. There must be a page at that address.

fields.name: parent_area
fields.label: Sits under
fields.description: The id of the area this one belongs to — for example "governance". Leave empty for a top-level area. This drives the sidebar tree, the breadcrumbs and the sub-area cards all at once.

fields.name: hub
fields.label: Show a card on the Resources hub

fields.name: external
fields.label: This area lives on another site
fields.description: Tick for an area whose "Page address" is a full web address. Its card opens in a new tab and shows "External" instead of a count.

fields.name: hide_type_chip
fields.label: Hide the file-type tag on every row
fields.description: Tick on an area whose documents are all the same kind of file. A "PDF" tag on every row of the page says nothing, and the room is better spent on the date.

fields.name: label_chips
fields.label: Name each tag on a row
fields.description: Tick on an area whose rows carry both a date and a reference number — the tags then read "Date 14/07/2026" and "Notification No. 2026/07/14/01", because two bare numbers side by side read as a puzzle. The words come from the page's own "Wording around the documents".

fields.name: doc_groups
fields.label: Groups of documents
fields.description: Each group is one headed block on the area's page. Use + to add one, the item menu to duplicate or delete, and drag to reorder.

fields.name: group_note
fields.label: Note under the group heading
fields.description: Shown on the live page, under the heading of this group.

fields.name: prose
fields.label: Explanatory text
fields.description: Shown above the documents in this group. Leave empty for none.

fields.name: documents
fields.label: Documents
fields.description: Use + to add one, the item menu to duplicate or delete, and drag to reorder. Deleting one here removes it from the page, from the search and from the count on the hub card.

fields.name: doc_type
fields.label: Kind of document
fields.description: Picks the icon and the tag on the row, and whether the link downloads or opens in a new tab. "Page on this site" is the one that opens in the same tab and shows no tag.

fields.name: href
fields.label: Link address
fields.description: A web address, a page of this site such as /resources-tech.html, or a mailto: address. Leave empty for a document that is announced but not published yet — the row shows without a link.

fields.name: lang
fields.label: Language
fields.description: Shown as a tag, for example Hindi. Leave empty for English.

fields.name: doc_note
fields.label: Note beside the title
fields.description: A short line shown after the tags on this document's row.

fields.name: updated
fields.label: Date tag
fields.description: Shown as a tag on the row, for example "Jan 2026". Free text.

fields.name: doc_ref
fields.label: Reference number
fields.description: The notification number, shown as a second tag beside the date — for example 2026/07/14/01. Leave empty on a document that has none.
